About

Kia ora. I'm Ants — a Dad, product, system and experience designer, people leader and runner.

Right now I'm creating digital and physical experiences for Z Energy — work that spans channels, maps journeys, and asks you to hold the full picture of how someone moves through a service. Before Z, I spent a decade at Xero across Product and System Design and Product Management, a lot of it keeping a design system honest as the product kept growing.

I cut my teeth in spatial design in the UK — architectural, retail, wayfinding, designing for the public realm — and that still shapes how I think about the way people move through and make sense of complex environments.

My approach is inclusive, collaborative and research-led. I keep stakeholders close, because decisions are easier when you're weighing evidence and keeping all of your audience central to the action.

Selected work
01

My Account

Z Energy · B2C · Lead Design (with AKQA) · 2023 – 2025

A secure home for every Z customer — and the foundation the rest of the ecosystem was built on.

The challenge

Z sold power plans, but customers had nowhere secure and logged-in to manage their account, monitor usage, or find their billing. For a modern energy provider, these weren't nice-to-haves — they were table stakes.

The approach

Over six months of interviews and surveys we validated real needs and pinpointed the gaps. Kano analysis separated the essential from the delightful; Jobs-To-Be-Done framed the work around what customers were actually trying to do; and low- then high-fidelity prototypes, tested early, surfaced friction and set a clear hierarchy of needs. I led design, working closely with development partner AKQA on the back end and the front-end system design.

The solution

A unified login — the July 2024 navigation refresh — gave every Z product a single front door. For My Account, rich JTBD insight shaped the landing page: billing and account management first, with usage and carbon-intensity insights above the fold and drill-downs for the curious. Most needs were met instantly; deeper exploration was a click away.

The outcome

With a small initial userbase, we watched the signals that mattered over vanity numbers — in-app funnels, session duration, the tasks people actually used, and the link between usage and support tickets. The product placed very little demand on support channels — a quiet validation the flows were clear.

The legacy

In 2025, Z Energy sold its My Account electricity-retail business to Meridian, so the product no longer runs. Its real legacy is the foundation — the ecosystem direction and a system-design-over-tech-stack approach that still lets Z present a united B2B and B2C experience.

02

Card Management Portal

Z Energy · B2B · Lead Design (with AKQA) · 2024 – ongoing

The B2B sibling — EV fleet charging, built on My Account's foundation.

The challenge

CMP serves EV fleet charging for business, with a very different mission: improve internal efficiency, move data seamlessly between suppliers, and integrate with the APIs operations depend on.

Building on a foundation

CMP inherited the hard-won work of My Account — proven navigation, an information architecture customers already understood, and adaptable components — so the team could focus on CMP's own challenges instead of reinventing the basics.

The solution

For busy fleet users, speed was everything. We elevated the two primary tasks — card activation and card ordering — front and centre, with page tabs for quick data interrogation. Unlike My Account, help and support were promoted into the primary navigation — though tellingly they've seen little use, a quiet sign the core flows are clear.

The thread

Together, My Account and CMP show one system serving two audiences from a single front door — B2C and B2B, each designed for how they actually behave.

04

Creating a Design System

Z Energy · Ampol Group · Design systems · Experience Design Lead · 2024 – ongoing

One source of truth for design across the Ampol Group — Ampol, Z Energy and Caltex.

The challenge

Two brands and several apps — Ampol, Z Energy and Caltex (NZ) — each carried their own patterns and components. The result was fragmentation, duplicated effort and mounting design, experience and technical debt, with no shared source of truth to keep things honest as the products grew.

The system

Leading a team of three, we established the design system as the single source of truth for digital design assets across the Ampol Group. It follows an atomic methodology: foundations — design tokens for colour, typography, spacing and elevation, a responsive grid and a semantic icon library — assemble into components, and components into patterns, all built on Figma Auto Layout so design maps cleanly to code.

At scale

The system spans roughly 90 design tokens, 250 icons, 140 illustrations and 260+ component variables — a toolbox that lets product teams deliver and innovate at speed across mobile apps, web and specialised interfaces.

A way of working

More than a component library, it's a way of working. I set the governance, contribution model, documentation and playbooks — with distinct paths for designers, engineers and product teams — and a process that runs from analysis and research through code, accessibility testing, and rollout with training and support. Adherence reduces design and technical debt and lifts delivery velocity, while a consistent visual language reinforces brand quality and lets non-designers build on-brand, accessible interfaces.

Launch & roadmap

Shipped v1.0 in September 2025 with systems for the Ampol, Z Energy and Caltex apps — introduced through playbacks and a live demo, and documented across SharePoint, Figma and Confluence. The roadmap extends coverage to web, web apps, Outdoor Payment Terminals and Barista apps, with an evaluative study planned to measure the value delivered.

Xero — Reporting & CIS

Xero · Product Design Manager & Senior Product Designer · 2012 – 2023

A decade at Xero — leading the reporting & analytics portfolio, and designing the end-to-end CIS tax experience.

Reporting — leading the portfolio

As Product Design Manager I led a team of six designers across Xero's reporting & analytics portfolio — cash-flow forecasting, data visualisation, the custom report builder, filtering, and the classic-to-new migration. With a mix of senior and junior designers, I led from different distances — embedding critiques, open sharing and constant customer research. Reporting lines ran to senior leaders, so the bar was high: high-quality design, evidence, and the diplomacy to carry proposals through executive scrutiny before a dollar of build was spent.

What shipped

The custom report builder — spreadsheet-level flexibility, built once and instantly reusable — alongside cash-flow prediction, data visualisation, a v2 back-end architecture upgrade, and system conformity across 50+ reports.

A leadership win

I'm proudest of growing a junior designer in a demanding ML/data space — backing her to take risks and design beyond the system's constraints to find something better.

CIS — end to end

Earlier, as a senior designer, I designed the end-to-end CIS (UK Construction Industry Scheme) experience — from invoice creation and tax accounting to HMRC reporting with dynamic rate polling, and the issuance of certificates to contractors and subcontractors. Hours of manual compliance, captured in minutes through one connected workflow.

06

Legible London

Applied Information Group, for Transport for London · 2008 – 2010

Pedestrian wayfinding for London — system design before it was a software word.

What it is

Legible London is a comprehensive, pedestrian-focused signage and mapping system, designed by Applied Information Group and later adopted by Transport for London. Its aim: reduce reliance on the Tube for short journeys by making walking intuitive, consistent and appealing across the capital.

My role

I designed the system components — the visual language and hierarchy of every element: the sign family and its materials (vitreous enamel, shot-peened steel, digital print under UV glass), typography tuned for every viewing distance, and an unambiguous cartographic language that gives pedestrians confidence of their place, orientation and distance to a destination.

The craft

At its heart was a "carto-engine" that generated heads-up maps at each sign's exact orientation — including 3D landmark buildings rotated to match how they actually appear from where you stand.

The legacy

My signs from 2008–2010 are still on London's streets — unchanged, hard-wearing, and useful even in the smartphone era. Legible London has since shaped wayfinding systems around the world, including here in Wellington.

07

Portland Design

Portland Design Associates · London · 2006 – 2008

Spatial and environmental design for retail at scale — Westfield and Inter IKEA.

Westfield

For Westfield W12 (London) and Derby I designed the wayfinding — signage, digital directory kiosks and their CMS, and navigation for vehicles from street to car park and pedestrians from car or transport onto site. Every element: typography, colour, pictograms and the digital information design.

Design under pressure

The hard part was often the negotiation — persuading architects that a piece of signage, far from cluttering their vision, serves the people moving through it. I'd rather someone move confidently through a beautiful space than feel anxious and lost in it. Safety and accessibility led; simplicity and repetition made it reliable; and everything was tested repeatedly, in all weathers, for uniform success. Much of that environmental treatment still gives W12 its signature feel.

Inter IKEA

For Inter IKEA at Matosinhos, Portugal, I built a complete design family and kit of parts — cartography, car parks and the full visual language, spanning information design, wayfinding and environmental graphics.
